sponsor_question: Will we hit the date, stay inside the cost envelope, and find out early enough to act if either changes.

outcomes.name: Forecast slip
outcomes.definition: forecast_ga − committed_ga, where forecast_ga = today + remaining_points ÷ trailing_throughput_per_day. remaining_points is the sum of story points on stories not in Done; trailing_throughput_per_day is points moved to Done over the last 14 sim-days ÷ 14, read by diffing consecutive daily snapshots. Before 14 days of history exist, throughput is the plan rate (total_points ÷ 70). If throughput is zero the KPI is reported broken with reason 'no completed work to forecast from' — never as zero slip. Once no points remain, the value is the day the last story reached Done minus the committed GA day.

source.query: issues under the program label: status, story points (customfield_10033); the epic's duedate as the committed GA; the sim clock for today; the snapshot from 14 sim-days earlier

outcomes.so_what: If the forecast slips past +5 days, the decision is cut scope or add a person to the critical workstream; past +10, the GA date is re-committed upward. Under +5 the date holds and nothing changes.

goodhart.gaming_path: Move stories to Done that are not done: remaining points fall and the forecast improves.
goodhart.counter: Reopen rate — stories leaving Done between consecutive snapshots — is reported beside it; any reopen in a week flags the forecast, and the decision on a reopen is to freeze the Done definition and add a review gate.

failure_modes: Throughput window straddles a holiday or an onboarding week: the forecast swings on a small denominator.
Points re-estimated downward mid-flight: remaining falls without work.
Denominator collapse: with few stories left, one closure moves the forecast by days.

outcomes.name: Cloud cost vs envelope
outcomes.definition: cumulative_actual − cumulative_plan through the last complete landed week, and cumulative_actual ÷ cumulative_plan as the percentage. The single-week view is the leading indicator weekly-spend-burn-ratio, not part of this number.

source.system: Cloud spend line (simulator spend.csv in the snapshot; a billing export for a real program)
source.query: week, planned_usd, actual_usd for every landed week
source.owner: TPM; Finance owns the source row

outcomes.so_what: Over 110 % of plan-to-date for two consecutive weeks: the decision is re-scope the pipeline (sampling, retention) or go back to Finance for the envelope.

goodhart.gaming_path: Defer ingest of a service to next quarter so this program's line looks fine.
goodhart.counter: scope-change-pct — a service dropped from scope shows there.

failure_modes: The spend line is a weekly feed that can silently stop; staleness is the common case, not the edge.
A misaligned week boundary mis-states plan-to-date.
A spike attributed to this program that was another team's.

leading.name: Scope change vs baseline
leading.definition: (points_added − points_removed) ÷ baseline_points × 100, where baseline is the sum of story points on stories present in the sim-day-0 snapshot, added is points on stories not in that snapshot, and removed is points on day-0 stories no longer under the program. Reported net, with added and removed separately.

source.query: issues under the program label: story points, presence vs the day-0 snapshot (created is informative only)

leading.so_what: Net scope over +10 % triggers a scope review with the sponsor that week: which stories are GA-blocking and which are not.

goodhart.gaming_path: Hide scope by not filing it — caught by the forecast when the unfiled work has to be done anyway.

failure_modes: Stories moved out of the epic read as removals.
Unestimated stories are invisible: the count of unestimated open stories is reported beside it.

leads.mechanism: Points added today are days of work the forecast has not absorbed; the sponsor's decision lead time is what this buys — a 15 % add with seven weeks left is recoverable, the same add with two is not.
leads.lead_time: same day for the number; weeks for the decision

leading.name: Critical-path slack
leading.definition: Over every blocks link whose downstream is on a chain to a story labelled ga-blocking and whose upstream and downstream are both open: slack = downstream.start − upstream.due. The KPI is the minimum, with the link named. No open link on a GA chain: no value, reported as such.

source.query: issues under the program label: Blocks links, start date (customfield_10015), duedate, status, the ga-blocking label

leading.so_what: Slack under 3 days on a GA-blocking chain: the TPM re-sequences or re-assigns that week. Negative slack: the downstream's dates are re-planned immediately.

goodhart.gaming_path: Push downstream start dates out to manufacture slack — which is slipping the schedule quietly.
goodhart.counter: forecast-slip-days — pushed starts flow into remaining-work timing.

failure_modes: Links entered backwards invert the sign.
A story without a start date drops out of the minimum silently: the number of skipped links is reported.
A late upstream with no re-planned due date under-reports; the transitive half of blocked share sees it.

leads.mechanism: A due-date slip on an upstream consumes slack first; the forecast only moves once the downstream fails to start and throughput on that chain falls.
leads.lead_time: the slack itself — at +10 days a slip is invisible to the forecast for ~10 days

leading.name: Blocked share of open work on GA chains
leading.definition: Points on open stories on chains to a ga-blocking story whose status is Blocked (direct), or whose upstream — transitively via Blocks links — is open and Blocked or past due (transitive), ÷ all open points in the program. Direct and transitive halves are reported separately.

source.query: issues under the program label: status (the Blocked status), Blocks links, story points, duedate, the ga-blocking label

leading.so_what: Blocked share over 25 % for three consecutive days: the TPM's weekly ask to the sponsor names the blocker owner — that is the escalation, not a dashboard colour.

goodhart.gaming_path: Leave a blocked story In Progress rather than mark it Blocked.
goodhart.counter: The transitive half catches it when the upstream is late; days-in-status on In Progress stories is in the drill-through.

failure_modes: A project without a Blocked status makes the direct half read zero: it must be reported not measurable, never zero.
Transitive blockage over-counts when an upstream is late by a day.

leads.mechanism: Blocked points will not convert to throughput this window; a rising blocked share precedes a falling trailing throughput by up to the window length.

leading.name: Weekly spend burn ratio
leading.definition: For the latest landed spend week, actual spend ÷ planned spend for that week (single-week, not cumulative). 1.0 is on plan. If planned spend for the week is zero, report broken with reason 'no planned baseline for week' — never zero or infinity.

source.system: Cloud spend line (simulator spend.csv in the snapshot)
source.query: the latest landed row: actual_usd ÷ planned_usd
source.owner: TPM; Finance owns the source row

leading.so_what: Over 1.2 for two consecutive weeks, the sponsor changes telemetry retention and sampling now to protect the envelope; a single week over 1.5 is escalated the week it lands.

goodhart.gaming_path: Shift ingest or storage load into a later week to keep any single week near 1.0 while total spend is unchanged.
goodhart.counter: cost-vs-envelope — single-week smoothing leaves cumulative variance visible.

failure_modes: Stale source: the row lands the Monday after, so overspend is seen up to a week late.
Plan drift: a mid-program revision to planned weekly spend resets the baseline.
Single-week noise: a one-off backfill spike reads as a burn problem when cumulative spend is fine.

leads.mechanism: Cumulative variance is the running sum of weekly gaps; the weekly ratio crosses its threshold before the cumulative figure does.

rejected.name: Throughput, trailing two weeks (points/week)
rejected.reason: The denominator of the forecast and reported inside it; demoted to the drill-through, labelled activity-derived, when the burn ratio took the fourth slot.

rejected.name: Throughput vs required run-rate
rejected.reason: slip > 0 exactly when throughput < remaining ÷ weeks remaining: the same inputs on the same day in different units.

rejected.name: Reopen rate
rejected.reason: Reported beside the forecast as its Goodhart counter by rule; a counter does not take a slot.

rejected.name: Stories closed per week / velocity
rejected.reason: The team's output count, not the program's result.

rejected.name: % stories with comments in the last 7 days
rejected.reason: The sponsor changes nothing on it; a TPM diagnostic.

rejected.name: % stories with dates populated
rejected.reason: The forecast's data-hygiene check; a drill-through item.

rejected.name: Open drift findings (count)
rejected.reason: Its content feeds the slack indicator; its count changes no decision.

rejected.name: Days since last status update per story
rejected.reason: A stalled-story conversation, not SVP altitude.

rejected.name: Trace coverage (% services emitting traces)
rejected.reason: The truest product outcome, and no source in the brief carries it; recorded so the successor program measures it.

rejected.name: On-call alert volume after GA
rejected.reason: The real outcome of an observability platform, not observable until after GA.

notes: Adopted set per docs/kpi/trees/simulated-program.review.md (2026-08-22): outcomes from the baseline with the agent's broken-with-reason wording; blocked share restricted to GA chains per the agent; weekly burn ratio from the agent; throughput demoted. The ga-blocking label and the 14-day window are RC1-300 decisions.
